State Update APIs

State in is updated by submitting candidate values into the pipeline through the FeatureCell API. Whether replacing state, merging partial updates, or streaming values over time, every update follows the same deterministic pipeline lifecycle before being committed by the State stage.

If you are familiar with Redux, replaceState() and mergeState() serve the role of dispatching updates. Instead of dispatching actions, you submit candidate state directly into the pipeline, where it is resolved, processed, and committed as an immutable snapshot.

Updating State

While the State Stage is responsible for committing finalized pipeline outcomes, state updates are initiated through the FeatureCell API. A FeatureCell exposes three distinct mechanisms for submitting state updates into the pipeline: replaceState(), mergeState(), fromStream(), fromDeferred(), fromObservable(), and fromPromise().

Each mechanism enters the pipeline through a different admission path but ultimately resolves, processes, and commits state through the same deterministic pipeline stages.

Mental Model

Updating state in follows a simple pattern:

  • Submit a candidate value using a FeatureCell update API.
  • The pipeline resolves and processes the candidate deterministically.
  • The State stage commits a single immutable snapshot.

The difference between update mechanisms lies in how the candidate state is produced—not in how it is committed.

Selecting an Update Mechanism

  • Use replaceState() when the incoming value represents a complete, authoritative replacement.
  • Use mergeState() when applying partial or incremental updates to existing committed state.
  • Use fromStream() when state must react continuously to an external observable source.

Bridge APIs exist primarily for migration and interoperability scenarios. In most cases, submitting values directly to replaceState() or mergeState() provides the most direct and predictable update path.

Execution Guarantees

  • All values submitted to replaceState(), mergeState(), or fromStream() enter the pipeline through standard admission.
  • All inputs are processed by the Resolve stage before downstream execution.
  • The State stage commits exactly one authoritative state snapshot per execution.
  • Committed state remains immutable once emitted.

The difference between these mechanisms lies in how candidate state is produced: replaceState() forwards a resolved value directly, mergeState() combines it with existing committed state using a Merge behavior, and fromStream() produces repeated candidate updates over time.

Regardless of admission path, state commitment remains centralized and deterministic within the State stage.

Pipeline Position

Update APIs do not commit state directly. They produce candidate input that enters the pipeline before the Resolve, operator, filter, and reducer stages. Final commitment occurs exclusively within the State stage.

This separation ensures that all updates—regardless of source—are processed uniformly and committed exactly once.
